Name of the Surah

• It is called al-Ghashiyah (the Overwhelming), because it opens with mention of al-Ghashiyah, namely the Resurrection, which will envelop people on that Day.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• To make the Day of Resurrection awe-inspiring, by mentioning the punishment that will befall those who opposed (the commands of Allah): those with humiliated faces; and the reward of those who followed (the truth): those with joyful, radiant faces.

• To mention the proofs and evidences that point to the great power of Allah, which necessitates His Oneness, coupled with a rebuke to those who have not been guided by those signs, though they lie before their eyes; and to strengthen the Prophet ﷺ in his call and that he should not concern himself with the aversion of the polytheists, for their reckoning rests with Allah.

[Tafsir]

Has the news of the Overwhelming Event reached you, O Messenger, the Resurrection that will envelop people with its terrors?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 88, verse 2–7:

On that Day, the faces of the disbelievers will be humiliated by punishment and worn out by toil and fatigue. They will be scorched by a fire of intense blaze, and they will be given drink from a spring that has reached the utmost of heat. The people of the Fire will have no food except from a plant of thorns that clings to the ground; it is among the worst and most loathsome of foods. It will neither nourish the body of the one who eats it nor relieve his hunger or keep him alive.

Faces that Day will be full of delight, pleased with their striving (in the Hereafter) for having done good deeds in the world. (They will be) in a lofty garden, elevated in place and rank, where they will not hear a single word of idle talk. In it is a flowing spring. In it are raised couches, and goblets set out ready for those who drink, and cushions arranged in rows, one beside the other, and many spread-out carpets.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 88, verses 17–20:

Will they not then look at the camels, how they were created in this wondrous form? And at the sky, how it was raised up in this marvelous elevation? And at the mountains, how they were set firmly in place, so that stability and steadiness came to the earth through them? And at the earth, how it was spread out and made level?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 88, verse 21–22:

So admonish them, O Messenger, those who turn away, with what you have been sent with to them, and do not grieve over their aversion. You are only an admonisher for them; it is not incumbent upon you to compel them to faith.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 88, verse 21–22:
